contract.interface:
For finite graph G with n vertices and max degree D>=1, rational real symmetric strictly row-diagonally-dominant A and symmetric C with graph-supported off-diagonals, define V(x)=x^T A x/2+a sum_i x_i^4/4+c sum_edges[(x_i+x_j)^4+(x_i-x_j)^4]/4 and W=x^T C x/2, a,c>0. Paired quartics are actual target interactions. The output is L=log[Z(i)/Z(0)] continued analytically from zero for Z(zeta)=integral exp(-V+zeta W), with absolute additive epsilon error. It is not an arbitrary principal branch; L/n is a weaker intensive output. C need not have low rank.

A rationally acquired coefficient certificate supplies an open zeta rectangle |Re zeta|<u0, |Im zeta|<v0 with v0>1 and tube |Im z_i|<=r. Set m=min_i(Aii-sum_{j!=i}|Aij|), c1=max_i sum_j|Cij|, c2^2=max_i sum_j Cij^2, m*=m-u0 c1, theta*=min(3a/(1+2D),3c). Require lambda=m*-(3a+24cD)r^2>0 and eta=m*r-(a+8cD)r^3-v0^2 c2^2/(4r theta*)>0. Concave feasibility in r^2 plus rational bracketing acquires a radius; no hidden mixing or root oracle is supplied. Failure of this sufficient certificate is not a hardness theorem.

Horizontal real-noise complex Langevin remains in the tube and is strongly accretive. The implicit resolvent R+h grad S_zeta(R)=w contracts by (1+h lambda)^-1. Finite-chain parameter holomorphy, moment bounds, stationary limits and strong order-one convergence give holomorphic observable means f_O. On a real interval the process has the positive Gibbs law. The identity theorem extends Z f_O=integral O exp(-S) without first dividing by possibly zero Z. For O=W, Z'=Z f_W proves zero-freeness and L=i integral_0^1 f_W(it)dt. Stability alone does not prove this identity; the source's contracting wrong-cycle example computes the wrong second moment. This is a source-reported proof candidate built on established complex-Langevin and analytic-continuation methods.

At bounded degree/local coefficients and fixed positive margins, analytic quadrature uses O(log(n/epsilon)) nodes, O(n epsilon^-2 log(M/delta)) endpoints per node, O(n epsilon^-1 log(n/epsilon)) steps and O(n) sparse drift cost, for ideal tilde-O(n^3 epsilon^-3) absolute-L work, with root, bit and margin factors charged. Intensive L/n has ideal tilde-O(max(n,epsilon^-2)epsilon^-1) work but does not ensure relative partition-ratio accuracy. Workspace is O(n+nnz A+nnz C+|E|+M) numbers with precision charged. Polynomial inverse margin is not polynomial in an arbitrarily small margin's bit length. A projected monotone root construction and finite-bit Gaussian reduction are described, not implemented with certified end-to-end errors. Model coefficients must still be acquired.

Producer finite checks do not supply general proof validation. Ten-site transfer quadrature takes about0.126s versus23.975s stochastic, with no demonstrated advantage. At n=2, epsilon=delta=.01 the conservative proof constants require h about1.2851e-11, 28 nodes, 128455084912 endpoints and about3.3106e23 resolvent calls before inner bit work. This is an unexecuted sufficient upper recipe, not a necessary lower bound. Floating runs at much larger h do not implement that guarantee.

Ordinary onsite quartics with generic imaginary neighbor forcing fail the displayed bounded-tube construction; whitening complexifies the quartic and fixed translations do not remove phase. Curved tubes require compatible noise and Ito/divergence corrections. A new geometry must preserve the original integral, a positive real anchor, noise tangency, nonexplosion, moments, holomorphy, mixing and fully acquired costs. General applicability, historical novelty, practical certified computation and transformative capability remain unestablished.
